source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: How do combined hormonal contraceptives mainly prevent pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Estrogen gives negative feedback that suppresses follicle development and ovulation; progestin thickens cervical mucus.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 How CHCs work (PDF p. 49)
questions.quote: CHCs suppress ovulation or the release of an egg from the ovary.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A woman on rifampicin for TB asks about using pills. The nurse explains that rifampicin:
questions.rationale: Rifampicin and most anticonvulsants reduce CHC effectiveness; most broad-spectrum antibiotics do not.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 Drug interactions (PDF p. 57)
questions.quote: Certain antimicrobials (rifampicin)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which condition makes combined pills an unacceptable risk (MEC Category 4)?
questions.rationale: Migraine with aura at any age is Category 4; varicose veins, anemia, and past ectopic are Category 1.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 MEC categories for CHCs (PDF p. 54)
questions.quote: Migraine with aura at any age

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A 38-year-old who smokes 20 cigarettes a day requests pills. Her MEC category for COCs is:
questions.rationale: Smoking more than 15 cigarettes/day over age 35 is Category 4 for COC, patch, and ring.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 MEC categories for CHCs (PDF p. 54)
questions.quote: Women who smoke more than 15 cigarettes/day, aged more than 35 years

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A client's BP is 165/105 mm Hg. Regarding combined hormonal methods, she:
questions.rationale: BP ≥160/100 is Category 4 for CHCs; 140–159/90–99 is Category 3.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 MEC categories for CHCs (PDF p. 54)
questions.quote: Have high blood pressure (systolic of more than or equal to 160 mm Hg or diastolic of more than or equal to 100 mm Hg)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which symptom in a pill user requires immediate referral?
questions.rationale: Warning signs: jaundice, severe abdominal or chest pain, severe headache, eye problems, severe arm or leg pain.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 Referral (PDF p. 56)
questions.quote: Severe arm or leg pain (difficulty in moving)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Long-term COC use reduces the risk of which cancers?
questions.rationale: Protection against endometrial and ovarian cancer begins after a year and lasts at least 15 years after stopping.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 Lasting effects (PDF p. 54)
questions.quote: Decreases the risk of cancers of the uterine lining and the ovary.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A client starts COCs on day 8 of her cycle. What should the nurse advise?
questions.rationale: COCs started after day 5 need abstinence or a backup for the next 7 days.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 When to start COCs (PDF p. 62)
questions.quote: should practice abstinence or use a backup contraceptive for the next seven days

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: An exclusively breastfeeding mother wants pills. When may she start COCs?
questions.rationale: Estrogen may decrease milk; breastfeeding women start COCs at 6 months or when they stop breastfeeding.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 When to start COCs (PDF p. 62)
questions.quote: Breastfeeding women may begin COCs at six months postpartum or when they quit breastfeeding.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A mother who is not breastfeeding may start COCs at:
questions.rationale: Non-breastfeeding postpartum women may begin COCs three weeks after delivery.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 When to start COCs (PDF p. 62)
questions.quote: Postpartum women who are not breastfeeding may begin taking COCs three weeks after delivery.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A woman on 30-mcg pills forgot one active pill yesterday. What should she do?
options: Take it now; next pill on time
questions.rationale: For 1–2 missed pills (30–35 mcg EE), take one ASAP and the next at the usual time, even two in a day; no backup needed.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 Missed pills (PDF p. 63)
questions.quote: take one pill as soon as possible and then take the next pill at the regular time even if this means taking two pills in one day

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A woman missed three active 30-mcg pills in the second week. Besides resuming pills, she should:
questions.rationale: Missing 3 or more active pills requires abstinence or backup for 7 days.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 Missed pills (PDF p. 63)
questions.quote: should abstain from sex or use a backup contraceptive for seven days in a row

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A pill user vomits within 2 hours of taking an active pill. She should:
questions.rationale: Vomiting within two hours after an active pill: take another active pill.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 Vomiting or diarrhea (PDF p. 64)
questions.quote: If vomiting occurs within two hours after taking an active (hormonal) pill, the client should take another active pill.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: How often is a combined injectable contraceptive (e.g., Cyclofem) given?
questions.rationale: CICs are monthly IM injections; DMPA is every 3 months.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 Combined injectables (PDF p. 65)
questions.quote: intramuscularly injected once a month

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: What is the grace period for a late monthly combined injectable without extra protection?
questions.rationale: The CIC grace period is 7 days; later, give if not pregnant plus backup for 7 days.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 Delayed injection (PDF p. 72)
questions.quote: The grace period of CICs is seven days without the need for extra contraceptive protection.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Who may administer combined injectable contraceptives?
questions.rationale: CICs can be provided by a trained nurse or midwife; no pelvic exam is needed.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 Advantages of CICs (PDF p. 65)
questions.quote: Can be provided by a trained nurse or midwife

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which site must be avoided when applying a contraceptive patch?
questions.rationale: Avoid the breast area because high local estrogen can cause tenderness; rotate sites.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 Transdermal patch (PDF p. 77)
questions.quote: The breast or areas surrounding the breast must be avoided

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: How is the contraceptive patch used each cycle?
questions.rationale: Change the patch weekly on the same day for 3 weeks, then a patch-free week.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 Transdermal patch (PDF p. 77)
questions.quote: The patch is changed once a week for three weeks (total of 21 days), followed by a patch-free week.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A patch has been off for more than 24 hours. What should the client do?
questions.rationale: After 24 hours detached, apply a new patch (new change day) and use backup for 7 days; never tape it.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 Patch falls off (PDF p. 79)
questions.quote: If detached longer than 24 hours, a new patch should be applied

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which counseling point is essential for every woman using combined hormonal methods?
options: They do not protect against STIs
questions.rationale: Emphasize correct use, warning signs, no STI/HIV protection (use condoms), and quitting smoking.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 4 Counseling tips (PDF p. 58)
questions.quote: The fact that CHCs do not protect the client against STIs, including HIV, and that use of condoms is necessary.
